brief: Morgan Stanley's chief economist defends the firm's “Embracing Risk” call (overweight recommendations for equities globally) against heavy client pushback at its Asia Pacific Summit, noting a continued equity selloff the Friday after the conference. The reasoning chain: AI capex plus wealth-effect household spending is driving US growth, and US capex is fueling Asian exports as Asia's own capex cycle broadens toward self-sustaining. MS has less conviction on inflation but expects it to peak in Q1 next year then retreat, implying developed-market central banks hike less than priced; inflation has already surprised to the upside, and further one-off surprises would push rate expectations higher. If wrong, the outcome depends on the cause: an energy shock plus tighter policy causing a growth slump is risk-negative, while demand-driven inflation with pricing power would be a boon for equities (a nominal-dollar inflation hedge) and offset higher-rate drag. The path to end-2027 won't be smooth given geopolitical risk and fiscal strain (US shutdown/debt-limit risk, France). MS still reads the weight of evidence as growth staying solid, with sticky inflation alone not enough to derail the trend.
